Dental  Terminology                                              Event  Category:  Health  Science
…………………………………………………………………………………………………………………………
 
Eligible  Divisions:  Secondary  &  Postsecondary/  Collegiate  
Round  One:  50  Q  test  (60  minutes)  Digital  Upload:  NO  
Solo  Event:  1  competitor   
New  for  2026-2027
 Tiebreakers  have  been  reduced  to  ten  (10)  questions.  Editorial  changes  have  been  made.   
Event  Summary
 Dental  terminology  allows  members  to  gain  knowledge  and  skills  regarding  language  common  to  all  dental  careers  and  
specialties.
 
This
 
competitive
 
event
 
consists
 
of
 
a
 
written
 
test.
 
In
 
the
 
event
 
of
 
a
 
tie,
 
the
 
tiebreaker
 
questions
 
will
 
be
 
judged. It  
inspires
 
members
 
to
 
learn
 
about
 
dental
 
terminology,
 
physiology,
 
and
 
pathophysiology.
  
Sponsorship
 
HOSA-Future  Health  Professionals  appreciates  the  sponsorship  of  Dental  Terminology  by  the  American Dental  Education  Association. 
 
                                                            
General  Event  Information
 
General  Rules   Competitors  must  be  familiar  with  and  adhere  to  the  General  Rules  and  Regulations.  
Dress  Code  Proper  business  attire  or  ofﬁcial  HOSA  uniform.  Bonus  points  will  be  awarded  for  proper  dress.  
Competitors  Must  Provide  ●  Photo  ID ●  Two  #2  lead  pencils  (not  mechanical)  with  an  eraser  ●  Neon  colored  foam  earplugs,  NOT  earbuds,  for  noise  control  (optional)  HOSA  Conference  Staff  will  provide  equipment  and  supplies  listed  in  Appendix  I.  
Ofﬁcial  References   The  references  below are  used  in  the  development  of  the  test  questions:  ●  Kindle,  Calista  and  Dofka.  Charline  M.   Dental  Terminology.   Cengage  Learning.   Latest  edition. ●  Nelson,  Stanley  J.  Wheeler’s  Dental  Anatomy,  Physiology  and  Occlusion,  Elsevier.   Latest  edition  
ROUND  ONE-  Test
 
Test  Instructions  All  competitors  will  be  given  a  test  and  test  answer  sheet.  The  written  test  will  consist  of  50  multiple  choice  questions  in  a  maximum  of  60  minutes.  See  test  instructions  here. Two  sets  of  ﬁve  (5)  ﬁll-in-the-blank  tiebreaker  questions  will  be  administered  with  the  original  test.  Correct  spelling  is  required  for  an  item  to  be  considered  correct.  Tiebreakers  should  be  written  in  the  space  provided  in  the  test  booklet.  
Time  Remaining  Announcements  
There  will  be  NO  verbal  announcements  for  time  remaining  during  ILC  testing.   All  ILC  testing  will  be  completed  in  the  Testing  Center,  and  competitors  are  responsible  for  monitoring  their  own  time.  
 Dental  Terminology  ILC  Guidelines  (September  2026)         Page  1  of  2  The  expectation  is  that  competitors  read  and  are  aware  of  all  the  content  within  these  guidelines  and  associated  links.  Successful  competitors  will  study  all  links  for  the  detailed  information.   

Written  Test  Plan  The  test  plan  for  the  Dental  Terminology  Test  is:  ●  Comprehensive  Dental  Care  and  Dental  Specialties  -  30%  ○  General  Dentistry  ○  Oral  and  Maxillofacial  Surgery  ○  Cosmetic  Dentistry  ○  Pediatric  Dentistry  ○  Prosthodontics  ○  Endodontics,  Orthodontics,  &  Periodontics  ○  Implant  Dentistry  ○  Dental  ofﬁce  laboratory  and  equipment  ●  Dental  Instruments  -  10%  ●  Pharmacology  &  Pain  Management  -  10%  ●  Emergency  Care  -  10%  ●  Tooth  Restorations  -  10%  ●  Head  and  Neck  Anatomy  -  10%  ●  Radiography  -  10%  ●  Dental  Laboratory  Materials  and  Procedures  -  10%  
Sample  Test  Questions  1.  What  ridge  occurs  on  the  occlusal  surface  of  posterior  teeth  at  a  point  where  two          triangular  ridges  meet?  (Dofka  pp  52)  A.  Marginal  ridge  B.  Oblique  ridge  C.  Transverse  ridge   D.  Triangular  ridge   2.  What  is  a  small  elevation  on  a  portion  of  a  crown  produced  by  an  extra  formation  of  enamel?  (Nelson  pp  7)  A.  Ridge  B.  Cingulum  C.  Tubercle  D.  Cusp   What  is  a  cowhorn?  (Nelson  pp  285)  A.  Extraction  forceps  B.  Apical  forceps  C.  Root  Elevator  D.  Maxillary  Elevator   
Final  Scoring 
 In  the  event  of  a  tie,  successive  sets  of  ﬁve  (5)  tiebreaker  questions  will  be  judged  until  a  winner  is  determined.  Correct  
spelling
 
is
 
required
 
for
 
an
 
item
 
to
 
be
 
considered
 
correct
 
in
 
the
 
tiebreaker.
 
  
Future  Opportunities The  HOSA  Scholarship  program  has  funding  available  for  HOSA  members  who  have  an  interest  in  various  health  careers!   The  application  process  begins  January  1,  2027,  and  can  be  found  here: https://hosa.org/scholarships/.   Graduating  from  high  school  or  completing  your  postsecondary/collegiate  program  does  not  mean  your  HOSA  journey  has  to  
end.
